MSFT.rationale: MSFT presents a strong fundamental case: Q3 FY26 revenue of $82.9B (+18.3% YoY), operating income of $38.4B growing steadily QoQ ($37.96B→$38.27B→$38.40B), operating margins of 46.3%, and OCF of $46.68B exceeding net income by 47%. The balance sheet is a fortress with $38B net cash and D/E of 0.119. The franchise is best-in-class: 87.5% enterprise productivity share, Azure at 20-21% cloud share growing 40% YoY, and AI revenue at a $37B annualized run rate (up 123% YoY). Commercial RPO of $627B (+99%) provides extraordinary revenue visibility. Valuation has compressed meaningfully — PE at 29.0x sits near the bottom of its 1-year range (25.4-42.8x), representing ~29% multiple compression from peak despite no fundamental deterioration. PEG of ~1.26x is reasonable for a high-quality compounder. However, the score is capped below +0.5 by three factors: (1) the $190B annualized capex trajectory introduces structural capital intensity risk and the market's negative reaction to the Q3 earnings beat (stock fell ~5%) signals legitimate concern about returns on incremental capital; (2) earnings yield of 3.4% sits below the 10Y Treasury yield of 4.4%, creating a -100bps spread that constrains re-rating in the current rate regime; (3) Copilot adoption at only 3% penetration (15M of 450M M365 seats) and the loss of OpenAI exclusivity introduce execution uncertainty on the AI monetization path. The Q3 earnings beat and Azure's 40% growth provide a near-term positive signal, but the capex guidance increase and competitive cloud dynamics (Google Cloud +63%, AWS accelerating) temper the catalyst. Net: excellent franchise at a historically attractive but not deeply discounted valuation, with macro headwinds (rates, oil at $108.64) capping upside.
